text:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher node group us-west-2 reported sustained tail latency > 2s and rapid KV slab growth. Pager fired for oncall. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/continuous-batcher

ops-bot: autoscale alerted: queue-depth spike on cb-pool-3, microbatch size trending up to 64, eviction-count++ (logs attached). Paging: @samir oncall.

samir: on it, paging in SRE. starting triage. any immediate rollback option?

maya: looking now. quick summary: KV slab growth looks like a write amplification loop when microbatch > 32 under high concurrency. metrics: evictions_per_min jumped from 2 -> 350 in 3m. 99p latency jumped to 2.5s.

liam: can we throttle continuous-batcher at the router level? cheap mitigation: cap microbatch to 8 and lower batch window.

maya: agree. trying config hotpatch: set `max_microbatch_size=8` and `batching_window_ms=10` for affected pool.

samir: do it and roll back any long-running prefix cache entries. which nodes to touch?

liam: I'll patch the control plane now. command: ```bash
# apply hotfix to cb-pool-3 config
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \ 
  https://control.redwood.internal/pools/cb-pool-3/hotpatch \ 
  -d '{"max_microbatch_size":8,"batching_window_ms":10}'
```

liam: patch returned 200, pushing config to 3 nodes (rolling). watching.

ops-bot: config push acknowledged. rollout: node-17 -> node-22 -> node-24. healthchecks enabled.

maya: also triggered a targeted KV eviction to drain large prefix keys: ```bash
redis-cli -h kv-usw2 FLUSHKEYPREFIX user_cache:large_prefix_ --force
```

emily: heads-up — we've seen elevated 5xx for a small set of hosted customers on model-ddp-13b. Support loop notified.

samir: what's customer impact magnitude?

maya: preliminary: 3 customers (~0.7% of total qps) experienced >40% error rate during the spike window. overall platform 5xx increased ~2.2% for 12 minutes.

liam: after node-17 rolled, latency started to creep down. node-22 rolling now. no new evictions reported from node-17.

ops-bot: metric snapshot: evictions_per_min 350 -> 18 in 5m post-hotpatch. qps stable.

samir: good. mark mitigation in runbook and start incident channel for postmortem notes. assign a temp owner for investigation.

nora: I'll own the postmortem. first actions: correlate workload patterns, check prefix sizes, validate batching heuristics, and test a synthetic high-concurrency run in staging with microbatch=32 to reproduce.

emily: support update sent to affected customers: short note + apology, we are throttling internal batching to restore availability. tickets created (T-4012, T-4013, T-4014).

maya: follow-up hotpatch candidate: add guard in continuous-batcher to reject microbatch > 16 when concurrency > 5000 OR evictions rate > 50/min. I'll open a PR and link in the postmortem.

liam: taking logs and heapstats for the 3 nodes and saving to /mnt/incidents/2387654321/ forensics.tar.gz

samir: thanks. leaving a short blameless timeline in thread for handoff. I'm handing over to @nora for investigation; I'll remain reachable for questions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, customer impact reduced. Severity moved to S2.

nora: copying next steps into the incident tracker and a scheduled working session tomorrow 09:00 UTC. tagging infra and runtime teams.

samir: resolved the pager for now. closing the active paging loop. will follow up on postmortem ownership and ETA. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
